newsitem.title: INDIA: India stocks close higher, Bombay index up 1.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: India stocks close higher, Bombay index up 1.6 pct.

text.p: ** India shares finish with small gains after
weak start in speculator-driven trade, action confined
to pivotals
** Bombay's benchmark index up 53.41 points or 1.6 percent,
at 3,377.63, above day's low of 3,316.16
** National bourse 50-stock index up 10.10 pts to 958.30 on
last day of weekly account
** Delhi index up 1.8 pct at 726.01, Calcutta index gains
1.37 pct to 441.35 and Madras 0.79 pct to 3,262.95
** Shares of Gujarat Ambuja Cement rise 3.54 pct ahead of
first half results due on Wednesday
India shares staged a late recovery on Tuesday helped by short-covering and scattered buying at lower levels, dealers said.
End-of-account trade at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) forced speculators to cover short-sold positions, they said.
"I feel people were short in the market and covered up on the last day of settlement...," said Sanjay Vaid, chief dealer at brokerage Lloyds Securities.
The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) top index rose 53.41 points to close at 3,377.63 after slumping to 3,316.16 in early trade. Net volume totalled 7.27 billion rupees.
Dealers said they were not convinced of the strength of Tuesday's price rally which came on the back of a near six percent fall in the Bombay index over the last two sessions.
"It was purely speculator driven. Big buy orders in a market that lacked any buying support spurred the rise in share prices," said a dealer at an institutional brokerage.
State Bank of India, Reliance and Tata Iron & Steel Company Ltd led the rally at the BSE and ended above their comparative prices at the rival NSE.
Tuesday is the last day of weekly account at the NSE.

Shares of top cement firm, Gujarat Ambuja jumped 8.50 rupees, or 3.54 percent, to 248.50 rupees at the Bombay bourse in volume of 238,740 shares. The company is due on Wednesday to announce its first half results ending December 1996.
Analysts said they expect Ambuja to report a net profit between 475-500 million rupees in the first six months, up 16-22 percent from a net of 409.7 million in the year-ago period.
A meeting of the Securities & Exchange Board of India with major bourses to discuss uniform trading cycles for all exchanges was still in progress, officials said.
-- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265 9000
